## Personality

Wilfred Mott is driven by a desire to enter politics. His primary goal is to serve as a member of Parliament.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XXX. The Regent’s Class Is Organized P21](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0021)_

## Goals

- intends to enter politics to serve as a member of Parliament  <sub>[v1 CHAPTER XXX. The Regent’s Class Is Organized P21](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0021)</sub>

## History

Wilfred Mott previously fought and defeated [Elias Purdy MacKinnon](../character/elias-purdy-mackinnon.md) after Elias made a derogatory comment about [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md) Harcourt's recitations. He also once praised [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md) to his mother, declaring that she was the cleverest female student in the entire school.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot P22](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0022), [v1 CHAPTER XXVI. The Story Club Is Formed P2](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0002)_

## Background by volume

**Volume 1**

- challenged Arty Pettigrew to leap across a well during a Mayflower picking outing  <sub>[v1 CHAPTER XX. A Good Imagination Gone Wrong P1](../source/v01-c20.md#nw-v01-c20-p0001)</sub>
- claimed his grandmother saw his deceased grandfather herding cows a year after burial  <sub>[v1 CHAPTER XX. A Good Imagination Gone Wrong P29](../source/v01-c20.md#nw-v01-c20-p0029)</sub>
- fought and defeated Elias Purdy MacKinnon over a remark about Nell Harcourt  <sub>[v1 CHAPTER XXVI. The Story Club Is Formed P2](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0002)</sub>
- told his mother that Nell Harcourt was the cleverest female student in school  <sub>[v1 CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot P22](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0022)</sub>

**Volume 2**

- penned local newspaper pieces in the past  <sub>[v2 XXIV A Prophet in His Own Country P0](../source/v02-c24.md#nw-v02-c24-p0000)</sub>
